title: Topic 17 | Friction forces and the inclined plane

questions.text: A traffic police officer found that the braking mark of a car on asphalt is 40 m long. If the coefficient of friction between the wheels and the asphalt is 0.5, at what speed was the car travelling? (km/h)
A body of mass 1 kg lies on a horizontal plane. A horizontal force of 2 N acts on the body. If the coefficient of friction is 0.3, determine the friction force.
A body of mass 10 kg lies on a horizontal plane. A force of 50 N directed at an angle of 30° to the horizontal acts on the body. If the coefficient of friction is 0.2, determine the friction force.
A body of mass 8 kg moves uniformly along a table under an applied force. What is the value of this horizontal force?
A block of mass 3 kg is pulled uniformly along a horizontal board by a horizontal spring. If the spring has stretched by 5 cm, what is its stiffness?
A body of mass 2 kg moves along a horizontal surface under a horizontal force with an acceleration of 2 m/s². If the coefficient of friction is 0.2, find the magnitude of the force.
With what maximum acceleration must a truck move so that the load in its body does not slide?
Determine the tension in the rope when a sled of mass 6 kg moves at constant speed. tanα = 0.75, μ = 0.3.
What acceleration does a sled of mass 6 kg acquire when pulled with a force of 20 N directed at an angle of 30° to the horizontal?
A block of mass 2.8 kg moves upward along a vertical wall. sinα = 0.6 and μ = 0.4. Find the acceleration of the block.
A body slides uniformly down an inclined plane. If the coefficient of friction is 0.2, what is the cotangent of the angle of inclination of the plane to the horizontal?
Compare the friction forces for two inclined planes with angles of inclination of 30° and 60°. μ = 0.8.
A body slides down an inclined plane of height 3 m and length 5 m. μ = 0.5. Find the acceleration.
A body is given a push so that it moves up an inclined plane. h = 4 m, l = 5 m, μ = 0.5. Find the magnitude of the acceleration.
The height of an inclined plane is 3 m, its length is 5 m and μ = 0.6. Find the ratio of the accelerations for motion up and down.
A body slides down an inclined plane of height 5 m and inclination angle 45°. μ = 0.19. Find the speed at the end of the descent.
A body slides down an inclined plane of height 5 m and length 13 m. μ = 0.4. Find the time of motion.
A small puck slides down an inclined plane with an inclination angle of 30° at constant speed. How long will it take to slide down an inclined plane of height 2.5 m and inclination angle 60°?
Find the minimum initial speed with which a body can reach the top edge of an inclined plane. h = 6 m, l = 10 m, μ = 0.5.
What minimum speed must be given to a block so that it can reach the base of an inclined plane of length 26 m and height 10 m? μ = 0.45.
A puck pushed up a 45° inclined plane takes how many times longer to slide down than to rise? μ = 0.8.
A body of mass 5 kg is lifted uniformly along an inclined plane with h = 3 m and l = 5 m. μ = 0.3. Find the force.
What force is needed to pull a load of mass 50 kg up an inclined plane with an acceleration of 1 m/s²? h = 3 m, l = 5 m, μ = 0.2.
A horizontal force is applied to a body moving up an inclined plane. The force is 2 times the weight. h = 3 m, l = 5 m, μ = 0.2. Find the acceleration.
A body on an inclined plane is pulled in the horizontal direction by a force half the weight. h = 3 m, l = 5 m, μ = 0.8. With what acceleration does the body begin to slide down?
